title: Peetambar Singh v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Saral Srivastava, J.; Sudhanshu Chauhan, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; EE to decide representation in accordance with law.
headnote: A 2 kW DVVNL consumer alleging successive unauthorised load increases to 3 kW and 4 kW is permitted to file a fresh representation. Without going into merits, the Executive Engineer, Mathura, is to consider and decide it in accordance with law after hearing, preferably within one month of the representation.
facts: Peetambar Singh, a consumer of Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited at Mathura, held a 2 kW connection (Account No. 1556043996) and claimed regular payment of dues. From June 2023 the recorded load was raised to 3 kW, which he paid till July 2024; in August 2024 it was raised again to 4 kW. Representations to higher authorities went unanswered. The licensee had earlier sought time to identify Supply Code clauses on increase and decrease of load.

holding_units.holding: Without going into the merits, the writ is disposed of. The consumer may file a fresh representation before the Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited, Mathura, within one month; that officer shall consider and decide it in accordance with law after notice and hearing, preferably within one month thereafter.
holding_units.flag: Order names no numbered clause; an earlier listing referred only to unspecified Supply Code clauses on increase and decrease of load factor.

not_decided.point: Whether the recorded load was illegally increased from 2 kW to 3 kW and then 4 kW, and which clauses of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 govern increase and decrease of load
not_decided.note: Writ disposed without going into merits; Executive Engineer to decide a fresh representation in accordance with law.
